senses.gloss: The rear section of the body of an insect, spider, or crab.
examples: A wasp's *abdomen* is joined to its chest by a thin waist.
The bee's black and yellow stripes run across its *abdomen*.
Spiders spin silk from glands in the *abdomen*.

senses.gloss: The fact that something is not there or does not exist.
examples: In the *absence* of any real evidence, the charges were dropped.
The *absence* of streetlights makes that road dangerous at night.
What struck me about the room was the *absence* of color.

senses.gloss: Rude and insulting language shouted at someone.
examples: The umpire took a stream of *abuse* from the stands.
She hung up when he started shouting *abuse* at her.
Players report racist *abuse* online after almost every game.

senses.gloss: A mark written above or below a letter to show how it is pronounced.
examples: Don't forget the *accent* on the e in cafe.
Spanish words often carry an *accent* over one vowel.
The keyboard has a shortcut for typing *accents*.

senses.gloss: The extra stress given to a syllable, a word, or a musical beat.
examples: In the noun 'record' the *accent* falls on the first syllable.
Move the *accent* to the second word and the sentence changes meaning.
The drummer put the *accent* on the offbeat.

senses.gloss: A detail added to a room or an outfit so that it stands out against the rest.
examples: The gray couch has two red pillows as an *accent*.
We painted one wall navy for an *accent*.
Gold *accents* run along the edge of every plate.

senses.gloss: A playing card marked with a single symbol, usually the highest card in a game.
examples: She turned over an *ace* and took the hand.
He was holding two *aces* and said nothing.
The *ace* of spades was missing from the deck.

senses.gloss: Someone who is extremely good at a particular thing.
examples: Ask Dana about the budget — she's an *ace* with spreadsheets.
His grandfather was a fighter *ace* in the Pacific.
The hospital's *ace* surgeon takes the hardest cases.

senses.gloss: LSD, an illegal drug that causes hallucinations.
examples: Half the band was on *acid* when they recorded that album.
He tried *acid* once in college and never again.
*Acid* was everywhere in the music scene of the late sixties.

senses.gloss: A synthetic fiber used to make sweaters, blankets, and yarn.
examples: The tag says the sweater is 100% *acrylic*.
*Acrylic* is warm and cheap, but it pills after a season.
She knits baby blankets out of *acrylic* so they can go in the wash.

senses.gloss: A single thing that a person does.
examples: Holding the door open is a small *act* of kindness.
The fire was ruled a deliberate *act*.
The policy does not cover *acts* of war.

senses.gloss: A law passed by a legislature.
examples: Congress passed an *act* banning the practice.
The new *act* takes effect in January.
Both *acts* cleared the Senate on the same day.

senses.gloss: Behavior that is put on to hide how someone really feels.
examples: She seems confident, but it's an *act*.
Don't fall for the helpless *act*.
He kept up the cheerful *act* until the last guest left.

senses.gloss: Fighting in a war.
examples: Her grandfather was killed in *action* in 1944.
The unit saw *action* in three countries.
He was wounded in *action* and sent home.

senses.gloss: A case brought against someone in a court of law.
examples: The family filed a civil *action* against the hospital.
A class *action* on behalf of thousands of customers is pending.
Both *actions* were settled out of court.

senses.gloss: A forward movement toward a place or position.
examples: The army's *advance* stopped at the river.
Nothing could slow the *advance* of the fire.
Farmers watched the *advance* of the desert year by year.

senses.gloss: An improvement or new development in knowledge or technology.
examples: *Advances* in surgery have cut recovery time in half.
The last real *advance* in battery design was years ago.
The new engine is a big *advance* over the old one.

senses.gloss: An attempt to start a romantic or sexual relationship with someone.
examples: She made it clear that his *advances* were unwelcome.
He apologized for the *advance* and left the party.
Employees can report unwanted *advances* to human resources.

senses.gloss: Tiny particles or droplets floating in the air.
senses.ru: аэрозоль, взвесь мельчайших частиц в воздухе
examples: The virus travels in *aerosols* that hang in the air indoors.
Volcanic *aerosols* cooled the planet for two summers.
Ocean spray puts a fine salt *aerosol* into the atmosphere.

senses.gloss: A very long time.
examples: I haven't seen Marcus in *ages*.
It took *ages* to get through security.
We waited *ages* for a table and then gave up.

senses.gloss: A business that provides a particular service for other people.
examples: We booked the whole trip through a travel *agency*.
The ad *agency* pitched three ideas and we hated all of them.
She found the job through a temp *agency*.

senses.gloss: The power to make your own choices and act on them.
examples: Kids need some *agency* over how they spend their afternoons.
The new rules left the nurses with very little *agency*.
The novel is about a woman claiming her own *agency*.

senses.gloss: An officer who works for a government department, especially in law enforcement or intelligence.
examples: Two FBI *agents* were waiting in the lobby.
The *agent* showed a badge and asked for identification.
Border *agents* searched the truck for two hours.

senses.gloss: A substance that produces a particular chemical or physical effect.
examples: Bleach is a powerful cleaning *agent*.
Yeast is the raising *agent* in most bread.
The lab tested several drying *agents*.

senses.gloss: Help or support given to someone.
examples: She found the switch with the *aid* of her phone's flashlight.
A stranger came to my *aid* when the car broke down.
Nobody offered any *aid* until the police arrived.

senses.gloss: A device or object that helps someone do something.
examples: My father finally got a hearing *aid*.
The teacher uses visual *aids* in every lesson.
A walking *aid* would make the stairs much safer for her.

senses.gloss: A state of watching carefully and being ready for danger.
examples: The hospital was on high *alert* all weekend.
Troops were placed on *alert* after the announcement.
The town stayed on *alert* until the storm passed.

senses.gloss: A warm yellow-orange color.
examples: The whiskey glowed a deep *amber* in the glass.
At sunset the whole valley turned to *amber*.
The kitchen is painted in warm *ambers* and browns.

senses.gloss: Facts or details that can be used to attack someone in an argument.
examples: The leaked emails gave his opponents plenty of *ammo*.
Don't tell her that — you're just handing her *ammo*.
Every small mistake became *ammo* for the other side.

senses.gloss: An amplifier that makes an instrument or a sound system louder.
examples: He plugged his guitar into a small *amp*.
The *amp* hummed until I moved the cable.
They rented two *amps* for the show.

senses.gloss: A therapist trained in psychoanalysis.
examples: He sees his *analyst* twice a week.
Her *analyst* suggested she keep a dream journal.
The *analyst* said nothing for the first ten minutes.

senses.gloss: A heavy metal hook lowered from a boat to hold it in one place.
examples: They dropped *anchor* in a quiet little bay.
The *anchor* caught on a rock and wouldn't come up.
Two men hauled the *anchor* back onto the deck.

senses.gloss: The person who presents a television or radio news program.
examples: The evening news *anchor* has been on the air for twenty years.
She started as a reporter and became an *anchor* at thirty.
Both *anchors* were in the studio on election night.

senses.gloss: Someone or something that gives a person stability and support.
examples: His grandmother was the *anchor* of the whole family.
Sunday dinner is the *anchor* of our week.
After the layoffs, that job was her only *anchor*.

senses.gloss: A very kind and helpful person.
examples: You brought soup? You're an *angel*.
The nurses on that floor were *angels*.
Her neighbor is an absolute *angel* about the dog.

senses.gloss: A particular way of looking at or presenting something.
examples: Try looking at the problem from a different *angle*.
The reporter needed a fresh *angle* on a very old story.
We studied the deal from every *angle* before signing.

senses.gloss: A hidden, selfish reason for doing something.
examples: Everybody kept asking what his *angle* was.
She's helping for nothing, and I don't see an *angle*.
There's always an *angle* with that guy.

senses.gloss: A person who behaves in a cruel or wild, uncontrolled way.
examples: Whoever did this to a child is an *animal*.
The crowd turned into *animals* as soon as the doors opened.
He eats like an *animal*.

senses.gloss: A way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficulty.
examples: More prisons are not the *answer* to crime.
There is no easy *answer* to the housing shortage.
She thinks money is the *answer* to everything.

senses.gloss: An urgent public request for money or help.
examples: The shelter put out an *appeal* for winter coats.
Their *appeal* raised forty thousand dollars in a week.
Police made a televised *appeal* for witnesses.

senses.gloss: The quality that makes something or someone attractive or interesting.
examples: The show has broad *appeal* across age groups.
I never understood the *appeal* of camping.
The car's *appeal* is that anyone can fix it.
